title: Tear Gas Exposure
symptoms: Burning eyes, difficulty breathing, skin irritation, coughing, disorientation
steps: Don't panic — move to higher ground where gas settles lower
Cover nose and mouth with a wet cloth (water, not soda)
DO NOT rub eyes — blink rapidly to flush tears
Rinse eyes with cold water or saline solution — tilt head sideways, let water run across eye
Remove contaminated clothing and wash skin with cold water and mild soap
If wearing contact lenses, remove them immediately (discard them)
Stand in wind direction — keep gas cloud behind you
Breathe slowly through wet cloth — short shallow breaths
Severe symptoms: difficulty breathing for >10 min, chest pain, blurred vision — seek medical help immediately
doNot: DO NOT rub eyes — causes corneal abrasion
DO NOT use oil-based products (Vaseline, coconut oil) — they trap chemicals against skin
DO NOT use water on skin if pepper spray (oil-based) — use dish soap or milk
DO NOT wear contact lenses to protests
DO NOT panic-run — conserve oxygen, move calmly
supplies: Carry: N95 mask, small water bottle, saline eye drops, bandana/wet cloth

title: Lathi Charge / Baton Injury
symptoms: Bruising, cuts, fractures, head injuries, internal bleeding
steps: Protect your head with arms — DO NOT turn your back
If hit, move away from crowd surge to avoid trampling
For cuts: apply direct pressure with clean cloth for 10 minutes
For suspected fractures: immobilize the limb, do not move it
For head injury: if dizzy, nauseous, or confused — seek IMMEDIATE medical help
Ice the area to reduce swelling (20 min on, 20 min off)
Take photos of injuries as evidence (send to a trusted contact)
doNot: DO NOT run in direction of lathi charge — move sideways/perpendicular
DO NOT remove embedded object from wound — seek medical help
DO NOT move someone with suspected spinal injury
DO NOT take painkillers that thin blood (aspirin, ibuprofen) for 24h
supplies: Carry: Small first-aid kit, antiseptic wipes, bandages, ice pack

title: Pepper Spray / OC Spray
symptoms: Intense eye burning, temporary blindness, coughing, skin burning
steps: DO NOT rub eyes — this spreads the oil
Flush eyes with cold water or saline for 15-20 minutes
Wash face with DAWN dish soap or baby shampoo (cuts oil)
Milk or yogurt can help neutralize — apply with cloth, not directly in eyes
Remove contacts immediately
Stand in fresh air — symptoms usually subside in 30-45 minutes
Wash clothing separately from other laundry
doNot: DO NOT rub eyes
DO NOT use water only on skin — oil needs soap to break down
DO NOT use oil-based lotions
DO NOT wear contacts or makeup to protests
supplies: Carry: Small bottle of liquid antacid (Maalox/Milk of Magnesia) — apply on skin to neutralize

title: Heat Exhaustion / Dehydration
symptoms: Dizziness, headache, nausea, dark urine, dry mouth, confusion, fainting
steps: Move to shade or cooler area immediately
Drink ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution) or water with salt + sugar
Loosen clothing and apply wet cloth to neck, armpits, groin
Lie down with legs elevated
If confusion or fainting occurs — seek medical help
doNot: DO NOT drink sugary sodas or energy drinks — worsens dehydration
DO NOT drink alcohol before/during protests
DO NOT ignore symptoms — heat stroke can be fatal
supplies: Carry: 1L water, ORS packets, wet bandana

title: Crowd Crush / Stampede
symptoms: Difficulty breathing, chest compression, panic, falling
steps: Keep arms up in front of chest — protect your breathing space
Move WITH the crowd, not against it
If you fall: curl into fetal position, protect head with hands
Try to get to the edge of the crowd
If possible, move diagonally toward the exit
doNot: DO NOT push against the crowd
DO NOT bend down to pick up dropped items
DO NOT scream — conserve oxygen
DO NOT stop moving — keep shuffling forward
supplies: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes. Keep elbows out to maintain space.
